Concept B — Balance bridge
The difference is the interface. Every unmatched item is a plank on the rec equation, hung under the side it moves and sized by how much of the gap it explains. Accepting lays the plank; at $0.00 the two sides meet and lock.
Arbor Analytics · 1010 Chase Operating ••4821 · Sep 2026 · Maya Patel, BD3 · frames 1440 × 900, left to right
B1 HERO
What Maya sees first
The page is the rec statement, drawn as a bridge: Statement ending → in transit / outstanding → Adjusted bank | DIFFERENCE | Adjusted book ← book adjustments ← GL balance. It’s the worksheet she already files, made live.
Each unmatched item is a plank hanging under the side it moves. Width is √impact with a 70px floor: at linear scale Meridian ($86.4k, more than the whole $82.7k gap) would leave 7 of 10 planks invisible. The √ / linear toggle keeps it honest.
The keystone answers “why is it off?” before any click: suggestions explain all $82,741.31, so if they’re right she lands on $0.00.
Default selection is the plank that explains the most. Four cash-neutral matches sit in their own tray: they can’t move the number, but a wrong pair is still wrong.
Trade-off: the bridge costs ~300px, so the detail below shows one item at a time.
B2 WHY
Resolving with the formula open
Two keystrokes lay the bank side: Adjusted bank is final at $9,029,866.58, and the ($191.31) left is exactly the net of the 8 book planks.
Every suggestion previews its effect on the bridge. The surprise sketching found: accepting AWS makes the difference bigger, ($191.31) → ($371.31). The gap isn’t monotonic (interest, Datadog and AWS push the other way), so the keystone says “explained”, never “closer”. Progress is the laid deck, not the number.
Why = weight × score per factor, summed to 88%. Evidence opens beside it with the transposed digits marked (42 vs 24).
B3 THREAD
Ember changes the UI from the thread
Each plank has its own thread with Maya, Priya and Ember. Maya asks @ember for an invoice; the tool call finds NTN-88213 in the AP inbox.
Two live changes, each with its own Revert: a new 96% candidate goes to the top, and “Expense now” is dropped. The plank on the bridge updates 72% → 96% and carries an Ember badge, so changes are visible from the overview too.
All candidates for an item move the same cash, so the difference stays ($3,997.98) until she accepts. Treatment changes; the bridge doesn’t.
B4 CASCADE
Items that don’t move the number
The tray is where cash-neutral work lives. Cascade: one $61,250 deposit, three receipts. Maya ⌘-clicks the four lines; the sum bar proves bank = books before M matches.
The bridge gives no reward here: the difference stays $5,602.02. So the tray keeps its own counter (3 of 4 confirmed), and “done” needs both the deck and the tray.
What I’d change after sketching: 4 of 14 items sit in a strip that looks secondary. In a busier month, matches could be most of the work, and the tray would need to grow into a real list.
B5 WHAT’S LEFT
⌘J answers in the bridge’s language
The page chat answers “what’s left?” in dollars: the remaining ($1,175.00) is exactly the two entries waiting on Daniel.
Accepted-but-unapproved planks are laid provisionally (grey-green deck, dashed card, DK avatar) and don’t count toward the difference, so $0.00 can’t appear before the controller signs. Complete stays locked.
Nudging Daniel is one click, from the chat or from the plank’s thread, where his original request still sits.
B6 DONE
Done at a glance
Continuous green deck, a lock at the joint, $0.00 in a tinted keystone, both piers at $9,029,866.58, tray 4 of 4. It reads from across the room.
The lower half becomes the workpaper Maya files (the classic rec statement) plus sign-off: 12 accepted as suggested, 1 found by Ember, 1 matched by hand, Daniel’s 2 approvals.
Complete reconciliation is the only primary action left on the page, in both the top bar and the sign-off card.
B7 PHONE
The bridge fits in a pocket
Daniel approves from his phone. The keystone and a mini bridge come first: grey-green segments are the entries waiting on him, and they add up to the whole difference.
Only his two cards follow, each with Maya’s note and the entry itself. Approve lays the plank and Maya’s bridge locks. The concept survives shrinking because the number and the deck say it all.
